text: Azure Resource Manager has Bicep sitting on top of it. AWS has its own direct equivalent: CloudFormation, a native Infrastructure as Code service built straight into the platform, not a third-party add-on. It answers the exact same declarative question Lesson 17 introduced, just for AWS resources instead of Azure ones.

Here's a real CloudFormation template in YAML. Resources is the required top-level section — every template needs at least one. AWS::S3::Bucket is the resource type, a fixed identifier CloudFormation recognizes, the same role Bicep's Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts plays for ARM. Everything under Properties configures that one bucket: a name, versioning turned on, and public access explicitly blocked.

Chapter 3's Boto3 version does the same job with two separate, ordered API calls — create the bucket, then separately turn on versioning. It works, but it has no memory of having run either one. The CloudFormation template declares both settings together, as one desired end state for one resource, inside one stack.

A stack is CloudFormation's unit: every resource a template declares, managed together under one name. Delete the stack, and CloudFormation tears down everything it created, in the correct dependency order, automatically. A Boto3 script has no equivalent concept — cleaning up means remembering, or re-reading, exactly what the script did, line by line.

aws cloudformation deploy creates the stack if it's new, or updates it in place if it already exists — the same create-or-update behavior as az deployment group create from Lesson 18. And aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift is AWS's own real, built-in drift check, comparing every live resource in the stack against its last deployed configuration.

ARM, Bicep, and CloudFormation all solve the same declarative problem Lesson 17 raised — end state, idempotency, drift detection — each one native to its own cloud. But native to one cloud is also exactly the catch. Next up: why this path's next course goes deeper on a tool that isn't locked to either one.
